parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A Hall probe is placed in a magnetic field. The Hall voltage is zero. The Hall probe is rotated
to a new position in the magnetic field. The Hall voltage is now maximum.
Explain these observations.

markscheme_points.text: it is zero when (plane of) probe is parallel to the (magnetic) field (lines)
it is maximum when (plane of) probe is perpendicular to (magnetic) field (lines)

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction that causes this behavior.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A Hall probe gives a maximum reading of $24\,\mathrm{mV}$ when placed in a uniform magnetic field of flux density $32\,\mathrm{mT}$.
The same Hall probe is then placed in a magnetic field of fixed direction and varying flux density. The Hall probe is in a fixed position so that the angle between the Hall probe and the magnetic field is the same as when the Hall voltage was $24\,\mathrm{mV}$.
The variation of the reading $V_{\mathrm{H}}$ on the Hall probe with time $t$ from time $t = 0$ to time $t = 8.6\,\mathrm{s}$ is shown in Fig. 6.1.
A coil with $780$ turns and a diameter of $3.6\,\mathrm{cm}$ is placed in this varying magnetic field. The plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field lines.
Calculate the magnitude of the maximum electromotive force (e.m.f.) induced in the coil in the time between $t = 0$ and $t = 8.6\,\mathrm{s}$.

$$\text{e.m.f.} = \text{....................................................}\,\mathrm{V}$$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
(36 mV corresponds to) 48 mT; use of 1.4 s or (8.6 - 7.2) s; E = ΔBAN / Δt; = − × × ×× 3 2 48 10 0.018 780 1.4 = 0.027 V
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.
